An import-time assertion pins the table to SPECS so it cannot drift onto a parameter that no longer exists. 15 tests.
findings.risk: An alias could shadow a real parameter of the same tool. Refused at import rather than at run time.

findings.evidence: ministral-3:3b scores 92% bare and 68% through GAFITAS. Of its 56 invalid calls in cohort 3, 44 are ERROR_BAD_ARGUMENTS, and 38 of those 44 (86%) are the identical string status='DONE"}\n```'. It wrote a well-formed finish inside a fenced JSON block and the argument value carried the block's closers out with it. Two of its 14 losses are classified FINISH_REFUSED with six and seven refusals apiece.
findings.impact: The single largest identified mechanism behind the canary's -24. A correct terminal call, refused as an unknown status, in runs that had already produced the answer.
findings.cause: status.strip().upper() normalises whitespace and case and nothing else. The value was the enum member plus the punctuation that closed the wrapper it was written in.
findings.fix: tools._enum_member(): the value must START with exactly one member of a CLOSED enum and everything after it must be structural -- quotes, braces, brackets, fences, commas, whitespace. One word character after the member and it declines, because DONE_MAYBE is a different word and guessing there would be a rescue. Never applied to free-text arguments: a file's content may legitimately end in a brace. 20 tests, including that a repaired DONE still faces every other finish gate.
findings.risk: A status the harness has not thought of that happens to begin with a member would be silently narrowed. Bounded by requiring the remainder to carry no meaning at all.

findings.evidence: Measured offline over the frozen fifty-case corpus, no engine invoked. Whole-repository ranking (before): recall@1 18/50, recall@5 32/50. Three of five slots reserved for files the objective itself names: 23/50 and 41/50. All five reserved: 23/50 and 43/50. Five cases gain rank 1 and NONE lose it under any scheme. The shipped implementation reproduces the predicted 23/50 and 41/50 exactly.
findings.impact: The correction for F-115. It moves the NOT_RETRIEVED floor, which is the largest loss bucket in all seven engines.
findings.cause: Stated in F-115.
findings.fix: orient.named_paths() -- a path-shaped token that RESOLVES to a real file, existence being the whole test, since constraining on a guess would hide the answer for good -- and NAMED_PATH_SLOTS=3 reserved in the shortlist, filled from the wide ranking after. Three and not five deliberately: two more cases is not worth giving up the only route to the answer when the named file is a red herring. When the objective names nothing that exists the ranking is byte-identical to before, which is the property that protects every mission that does not name a file. 12 tests.
findings.risk: This is a RETRIEVAL measurement, not an accuracy measurement. Conversion once the symbol is reached is 88-100%, so the direction is expected, but the size in accuracy terms is unmeasured and stays unmeasured until a discriminating GPU run.

findings.evidence: qwen3.5:2b: 91 ERROR_NO_TOOL_CALL turns in cohort 3. 82 of them emitted EMPTY content, and 80 of those 82 carry a recorded reasoning channel (median 392 characters, max 41 223). Only 2 hit the output budget, so this is not truncation. The model thought and then closed the turn without answering. Whether the call it had already settled on was sitting in that channel CANNOT BE ANSWERED from the sealed record, because the record held a character count and nothing else.
findings.impact: A whole cohort's worth of the cheapest engine's dead turns is undiagnosable, and the same instrument gap would hide it again next time.
findings.cause: F-100 sealed the answer channel and left the reasoning channel counted but unquoted.
findings.fix: reasoning_head (400 chars) and reasoning_tail (1200) sealed, with reasoning_elided stating what was dropped. The tail is the larger of the two because a model that settled on a call settled at the end. Bounded because one turn reached 41 223 characters and a cohort's evidence must not become mostly deliberation. 5 tests. This makes the question ASKABLE next cohort; it does not answer it.
findings.risk: Deliberately does NOT act on the reasoning channel. Reasoning is deliberation, and executing a call the model mentioned while thinking would run something it may have decided against. Measure first.

findings.evidence: F-101's residual question -- is a quarter of the served context ENOUGH -- answered from sealed evidence, no engine invoked. GAFITAS arm: the output budget was hit on 2 of qwen3.5:2b's 547 reasoning turns and 8 of granite4.2:3b's 278; no other engine emits a reasoning channel at all. Reasoning spend, measured in real output tokens rather than converted from characters: qwen3.5 p50 161 / p90 578, granite4.2 p50 1412 / p90 4083, against a budget of 8192. Bare arm, classified structurally: of 350 answers only 6 are long enough for an 8192-token budget to explain them (4 gemma3, 2 qwen3.5), 17 stop early at lengths no budget explains, and 6 are COMPLETE answers that echoed the prompt's own closing delimiter.
findings.impact: F-101 closes with a NEGATIVE result: at 8192 the budget is not what limits these engines on this corpus, on either arm. That removes the standing caveat that no cohort is fair until the budget is settled.
findings.cause: The budget was raised to a quarter of the served context by F-101 and that was enough. What remained was that nothing MEASURED whether it was, so the caveat could not be retired.
findings.fix: measured_reasoning_tokens (declared only from sealed telemetry, never from a family or a name), plus output_shortfall(), output_is_sufficient() and served_context_for(). The budget itself does NOT move: raising it on the strength of a measurement of the symptom would be tuning. What moves is visibility -- a deployment that cannot afford an engine's deliberation plus an answer now says so, and states the served context that would close it, instead of the run being recorded as the engine failing. output_is_sufficient() is three-valued: None means never measured, which is not the same as fine, and collapsing those two is how F-101 survived two cohorts. 15 tests, including that the verdict is identical for four engine names and that emits_reasoning_channel does not decide it.
findings.risk: measured_reasoning_tokens could be declared from a guess. Its docstring and this record both state the only admissible source; nothing enforces it mechanically.
